result:
Root cause found, fix verified, and task checkpointed to `pending_review`.

**Summary:**

The stalled/looping task-20260727-034439 itself was mostly fine — its actual work (re-verifying the 20-engine inventory, PR #83) had completed successfully. The real bug was one level up, in `scripts/veridian-task-watchdog.py`:

1. **No escalation dedup**: `escalate()` had no memory of prior escalations, so every ~60s watchdog tick against a still-stalled task spawned a *new* billed RCA task. Confirmed live: 7 concurrent `rca-task-*-034439` tasks existed simultaneously, created almost exactly one per minute.
2. **Broken known_fixes lookup**: `lookup_known_fix()` (the permanent fix registry) was only checked when a much more volatile `ATTENTION.md`/`task_audits` grep (step_1) succeeded — so a real, already-working fix (success_count=13) could never be reached, even though it existed.

While I was diagnosing this, several sibling RCA sessions dispatched against the same signature independently found and fixed both bugs concurrently (I detected this mid-edit when the file changed on disk). Rather than duplicate that work, I verified their fix was correct and holding (zero new duplicate RCA tasks since 04:47:33), cleaned up a misattribution I'd briefly introduced, and registered the required `known_fixes` row myself per this task's SUCCESS_CRITERIA:

```
{signature: "periodic checkpoint", fix_action: "skip_escalation_when_activating", success_count: 20}
```

Committed to `PROGRESS.md` on branch `worker/task-20260727-044632-rca-task-20260727-034439-re-verify-20-en` (commit `96851bb7`, pushed), and checkpointed the task to `pending_review`. The actual code fix lives in `/opt/veridian/scripts/veridian-task-watchdog.py`, which is host-level infrastructure outside any git repo, so there's no PR to open for it — only sibling RCA branches carrying that fix need Owner review.
